own_solution.law: Bernoulli gives v = sqrt(2gh), and continuity gives A dh/dt = -a sqrt(2gh). Integration gives t = (A/a)sqrt(2/g)(sqrt(h0) - sqrt(h1)). With A/a = (400/10)^2 = 1600, t = 323.2488 s. Increasing the hole diameter by q gives t(q) = 323.2488[10/(10 + q)]^2, with q in mm.
assumptions: The flow is quasi-steady, with atmospheric pressure at the free surface and jet.
The stated ideal-flow model applies, including negligible surface speed and a jet area equal to the hole area.
No water enters the tank during timing.
Widening by q means increasing the hole diameter by q.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with the drainage equation at the reported precision. Pre-timing diameter increases of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.9 mm give approximately 287.690, 253.151 and 228.267 s. Density cancels from the pressure-head and kinetic-energy relations; every listed density is admissible within the stated ideal-fluid model. The separate barrel and changes after timing have no causal path to the target. The cancellation expression has dimensions of time; its intermediate p is understood as the hydrostatic gauge-pressure head. Both explicitly claimed R/D minimal pairs retain 1.3 mm and change the relevant attachment or timing; the density variants also retain their number and unit.
